products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government laboratory, described on its site as a non-profit organization working across large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms and related fields. It states that since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China and Zhejiang University. The site also advertises global recruitment, including a 2026 campus recruitment round and a "North Star" talent program.

Its best-known AI product is InternLM, a Chinese open-source large language model tracked in the Chat and General LLMs category, with a note that it is used in academic research and that cross-border data review is advised. The site describes Intern-Robotics, an embodied full-stack engine intended to cover data, training and application for embodied intelligence, and Mobius, an open-source architecture aimed at long-horizon reasoning and scientific discovery. At the 2026 WAIC Science Frontier Forum the laboratory says it released ten joint science-intelligence results with universities, research institutes and industry partners in life sciences, materials science and deep space astronomy, along with a science discovery platform that connects science models, specialized agents, experimental data and embodied automation equipment across the research process from hypothesis generation to experimental verification.

On safety and method, the site describes a general-specialty fusion system with three layers: a base model layer, a fusion and coordination layer, and an exploration and evolution layer. It also sets out an "AI-45 degree balance law" for safety and performance over the long term, a causal path toward trustworthy AGI through alignment, intervenability and reflection, and risk management spanning evaluation, training, base, application and verification.
